doc.title: Mickey Roker interviewed by Michael Woods, Majesty of the Seas, May 31, 1995

title: First gigs in Philadelphia and move to New York in 1959
summary: He played R&B with King James and Jimmy Devine's High Five, then turned to jazz with Philadelphia players, and went to New York in 1959 to play with Gigi Gryce, Ray Bryant and Joe Williams.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Who did you get some of your first gigs with?

Well I played rhythm & blues in Philly with a band, a guy named King James. I did that for a year in a group with Jimmy Devine called the High Five. We had a band together for about a year, and then I decided that playing that way is so limited you know. So I devoted my life to playing jazz because it’s more free, it’s open you know, and you can express more rhythm. So then I started playing with people like Sam Reed, all these Philadelphia musicians, and Jimmy Heath and Jimmy Oliver. Jimmy Heath is the guy that introduced me to Milt Jackson years ago. So then in 1959 I went to New York to © Fillius Jazz Archive -2-
play with Gigi Gryce. So I played with Gigi Gryce for a couple of years, played with Ray Bryant for a couple of years, and then that’s when I joined Joe Williams’ band with the Junior Mance Trio.
